title: Non-Euclidean Gradient Descent Has Many Edges of Stability
summary: Recent observations that deep learning models train at the edge of stability have renewed interest in understanding stability properties of classical optimization algorithms. For quadratic objectives, standard gradient descent has a sharp stability threshold: it converges from every initialization when $η 2/L$, and diverges from every nonzero initialization when $η>2/μ$. For non-Euclidean gradient descent, the corresponding known guarantees are weaker: convergence holds for every initialization when $η 2/μ$.
